data.gender_notes: Fermo is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'fermus' meaning 'firm, steadfast'. In Christian tradition, Fermo can represent a strong and unwavering spirit. The name Fermo carries the meaning “Firm, steadfast” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Fermo usually hope their child will grow to embody firm, steadfast and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fermo total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: פֶרמוֹ
in_hebrew.meaning: מקום מוצק, יציב, או שם של קדוש
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם פֶרמוֹ נגזר משורש לא ידוע, אך ייתכן כי הוא קשור למילה 'פירמוס' בלטינית, שפירושה 'יציב' או 'איתן'. אין אזכור ישיר לשם זה בתנ"ך העברי, אך הוא עשוי להיות קשור למושגים של יציבות ואיתנות, שמהווים נושאים מרכזיים ביהדות וגם בנצרות. השם עשוי לשאת משמעות של 'מקום מוצק' או 'אדם איתן', המשקפים תכונות רצויות באדם.

in_greek.name: Φέρμο
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Φέρμο πιθανόν να συνδέεται με τη λατινική λέξη 'firmus', που σημαίνει 'στερεός' ή 'σταθερός'. Αν και δεν υπάρχει άμεση αναφορά στο όνομα αυτό στο Νέο Testament, οι έννοιες της σταθερότητας και της στέρεης πίστης είναι κεντρικές στο Χριστιανισμό. Το όνομα μπορεί να συμβολίζει την πνευματική ακεραιότητα και την ανθεκτικότητα, ιδιότητες που εκτιμώνται στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας.

in_latin.name: Fermo
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Fermo derivatum a latino 'firmus', significat 'stabile' vel 'robustum'. Quamquam non invenitur directe in scripturis christianis primitivis, conceptus firmitatis et stabilitateis sunt cruciales in traditione christiana. Nomen hoc potest denotare characterem robustum vel locum stabilem, reflectens qualitates quae in ecclesia christiana aestimantur.

historical_references.reference: Saint Fermo was a martyr in the city of Aquileia, who, during the persecution under Emperor Diocletian (284-305 AD), was sentenced to be buried alive in a pit. The story relates that he was miraculously rescued by a dove, which bore him on its wings to the surface. This miracle is commemorated in the town of Fermo in Italy, which is named after him.

Fermo was also the name of a 7th-century Lombard duke of Benevento who played an important role in the history of southern Italy. He was the son of Duke Arechi I and succeeded his father in 591 AD. Fermo was a powerful and ambitious ruler who extended his domain through military conquests and alliances. He is remembered for his successful defense against the Byzantine army and his role in the foundation of the ducal capital at Benevento.
